newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends lower after weak Aust. retail data.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends lower after weak Aust. retail data.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed lower on Friday after weaker-than-expected Australian retail trade statistics prompted a fall in the Australian currency.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6883/90 and at 67.50 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.6900/07 and 67.54 at the open.
The Aussie dollar dived over half a cent after the release of the retail data, which not only justified the rate cut in Australia last week but raised the prospect of yet another easing.
A bank chief dealer said the Australian retail data had encouraged the Kiwi lower "because of the anticipation that we are at a similar point in the (economic) cycle as the Australians".
The Kiwi was seen trading a 0.6870-6900 range overnight.
